source.citation: "Fort Dearborn History." Chicagology. Reprinting the address delivered by Hon. John Wentworth at the Fort Dearborn Memorial Tablet ceremonies, 21 May 1881, as printed in the Chicago Tribune, 22 May 1881; with the caption to a woodcut of Alexander Hesler's 1855 photograph, an addendum on the fort in 1850 signed Robert Fergus, and an extract from Chicago Magazine, Vol. 1, No. 1, March 1857.
what_it_does_not_supply: any hospital BUILDING inside the fort
any description of the 1816 fort's walls, blockhouses, palisade or sally-port that is unambiguously about the 1816 fort
the fort as it stood in 1835 (its two extended physical descriptions are of the pre-1812 fort and of the fort in 1850)
any plan, footprint, orientation or measured survey
the height, roof form or fenestration of any fort building
any evidence independent of wentworth_1881_fort_dearborn - it is the same text at a different address
what_it_supplies: NOTHING THAT wentworth_1881_fort_dearborn DOES NOT ALREADY SUPPLY, except the last three entries below - cite that record for the fort, not this one
commandant's quarters, brick, about 25 x 50 ft, at the north-west corner of the enclosure (1855 caption)
officers' quarters, wood, about 30 x 60 ft, at the north-west corner (1855 caption)
parade ground 80 x 200 ft (1855 caption) AND about 80 x 400 ft (Fergus, 1850) - a disagreement, not a figure
the sutler's building (key D) and the north gate (key E)
the 1850 arrangement: quarters west of the parade ground, artillery house, barracks and storehouse east
the sun-dial on an 8-inch square timber post about 2 ft high, near the parade ground's south end (1850)
the whitewashed rough-board fence about 6 ft high, pickets already removed (1850)
the kitchen garden in the south-west corner of the enclosure (1850)
the fort's use as a general hospital from 11 July during the 1832 cholera
Bvt. Maj. Joseph Plympton arriving 1 August 1836; the soldiers withdrawn 29 December 1836
J. B. Beaubien's purchase of the reservation, 28 May 1835, for $94.61
Beaubien's later residence at the north-east corner of South Water Street and Michigan Avenue, expressly after he left the John Dean house
the 1831 lighthouse authorised 3 March 1831, fallen in October 1831, soon rebuilt; Samuel C. Lasby first keeper
